study type: Retrospective analysis of routine health data
exposure: Routine monthly district health reports from 2016-2020
outcome: Reliability and usefulness of emergency obstetric care data
Maternal and neonatal care coverage indicators
Emergency obstetric and neonatal complications indicators (e.g., antepartum haemorrhage, pre-eclampsia)
Intervention indicators (e.g., Caesarean section rate, uterotonics use)
cohort: The study analyzed data from all institutional births reported in the Tanzanian District Health Information System between 2016 and 2020.
finding: The District Health Information System data showed mixed usefulness, with plausible institutional delivery and Caesarean section rates providing useful information on regional disparities and trends, but significant underreporting of obstetric complications and several interventions diminished data usefulness for monitoring.
mod_finding: The Caesarean section rate remained stable at approximately 10% of institutional births.
